notes:
Two no-op turns in ONE interactive GitHub Copilot CLI session (recorded on 1.0.78), separated by a /model switch window, then a clean /exit. WHAT THIS CELL DOES NOT ASSERT, AND WHY: the scenario's defining observable — two DISTINCT models, ModelName = model B after turn 2 — is not producible on this account and is deliberately absent from the phases below. Two independent walls, both evidenced in the cell's assessment and re-confirmed by this recording: (a) every concrete model id is refused by the plan — the recipe's `/model gpt-5-mini` step drew `Model "gpt-5-mini" can't be selected — only Auto mode is available on your plan` into the driver's stdout capture, because the CAPI model list is empty and only the literal 'auto' bypasses the availability check (app.js Gs(t){return t===cC}, cC="auto"); and (b) the hydra auto-router resolves ONCE PER SESSION, not per turn — session.auto_mode_resolved fires exactly once and both assistant.message records in this recording carry the same model (gpt-5-mini). So the switch cannot be commanded and will not happen by itself. agent_supports is therefore partial, following the gemini-cli sibling: the CLI HAS /model <id> and /model --session <id>, the environment refuses them. daemon stays full — it has no differing input to promote; were a switch to occur, session.model_change(newModel), session.auto_mode_resolved(chosenModel) and assistant.message(model) are all read by the parser and MergeMetrics' latest-non-unknown-wins would flip ModelName.

CORRECTION 2026-08-05 — THE SWITCH WINDOW IS TRUE SILENCE, NOT A SKIPPED EVENT. The pre-record spec claimed the window's no-flicker criterion was exercised against a REAL session.model_change line written by the recipe's `/model auto`, rather than against silence. The recording refutes that: events.jsonl holds exactly ONE session.model_change, at 07:30:05.890 — 4.7s BEFORE the first user prompt (07:30:10.597), i.e. the session-start line, not a slash-command line. `/model auto` wrote NOTHING, which makes sense: 'auto' was already the active mode on this plan, so there was no change to record. Both slash commands in the window are therefore local-only, and the window contains no transcript event at all. The no-flicker assertion is still real and still worth locking — it just asserts that ~11s of local slash-command activity produces no state churn, which is a weaker claim than the one previously written down. parser.go's Skip=true on session.model_change remains covered by unit tests, not by this cell.

WHAT IS ASSERTED IS REAL: two clean working→ready cycles on one session id, a silent switch window, TotalTokens monotonic across it (live per-message assistant.message.outputTokens increments folded as non-negative deltas), and ModelName a concrete Copilot label — not 'unknown', not the placeholder 'auto'. observations.model is UNPINNED: the router's per-session pick varies run to run (gpt-5-mini here; claude-haiku-4.5 seen in other runs) so no string can be pinned. cost/tokens ARE asserted; cost comes from the shared capacity price map, and a $0 result means a missing alias in core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go (that was the dotted claude-haiku-4.5 bug, now fixed). BIRTH SHAPE: copilot writes events.jsonl only at the first prompt, so processlifecycle.Scanner mints a transient proc-<PID> row (born ready) first and the REAL session arrives under a different id, born DIRECTLY into working because the file already holds the open turn (commit 3cde4f8d) — so session_birth and t1_start are ONE phase, as for basic-turn.

FINALLY, A NEGATIVE THAT MATTERS: this recording shows exactly ONE key in session.shutdown's modelMetrics. The 5-1 token-accounting cell's multi-model tail risk (drainPendingContribution attaches at most one queued contribution per event while shutdown is the transcript's last line, so a two-model session strands the surplus delta and under-reports input tokens) states its trigger as 'a recording shows two entries in modelMetrics'. That trigger is UNREACHABLE here for the two reasons above; if a copilot recording ever does show two keys, that caveat is what to re-open.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch — copilot creates session-state/<id>/ holding only workspace.yaml, so the 1s process scanner sees the process before any transcript exists
The real <session-id> session reconciles under a different id once events.jsonl appears on the first prompt, and is born DIRECTLY into working because the file already holds turn 1's open turn

Turn 1 completes back to ready on assistant.turn_end; that turn's assistant.message outputTokens is contributed live, so TotalTokens > 0 after T1 without waiting for shutdown, and SessionMetrics.ModelName is the router-resolved concrete label

`/model gpt-5-mini` (refused by the plan) and `/model auto` (accepted, but a no-op because auto was already active) both run locally with no LLM round-trip and write NOTHING to events.jsonl — see the correction in the meta notes. The session stays ready throughout: no working flicker, no waiting. This is the scenario's no-flicker criterion over a genuinely silent window.
Turn 2 user prompt → working on the SAME session id

Turn 2 completes back to ready; TotalTokens after T2 ≥ TotalTokens after T1 (monotonic across the switch window) and SessionMetrics.ModelName is a concrete Copilot model label — NOT 'unknown' and NOT 'auto', because turn 2's assistant.message re-stamps the serving model. The session never enters waiting: --allow-all means no permission.requested is written. NOT asserted: a model CHANGE — see the meta notes.
